SUNDAY MEETINGS AND OUTINGS
(19)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, Masonic Lodges have held picnics and other gatherings of their members and families on Sundays for many years and
other Masonic organizations have held similar gatherings and circuses
on Sundays; and
WHEREAS, most Lodges and other Masonic organizations do not
have sufficient funds to pay all of the expenses of picnics, outings.
trips to join with other Lodges, circuses and other family gatherings
and of necessity those participating must help to share these expenses;
and
WHEREAS, our laws do not permit such affairs to include the public and require that such affairs be limited to Masons and their families
and friends;
NOW. THEREFORE. BE IT RESOLVED that Section 326 of
the California Masonic Code be amended to read as follows:
326. Sunday M.eetings. No stated or special meetings of a Lodge
or the Grand Lodge shall be held on Sunday except for funeral
services and Grand Lodge cornerstone laying and dedication ceremonies for public school buildings or other exclusively public buildings directed to be held in the discretion of the Grand Master.
Lodges and other Masonic organizations may hold picnics, outings,
circuses and other family gatherings of their members, families and
friends for which tickets are sold. but there may not be any public
solicitation of sales of tickets to such affairs.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Annotations a. b, c, d and e
of Section 326 be, and they are hereby. repealed and deleted.
Respectfully submitted.

The Committee. on Policy and General Purposes:
R~s~lution N.o. 21 seeks to make it abundantly clear that a Lodge
may, 1f 1t so desires. publish an advertisement in a local newspaper to
announce the time and place of Lodge meetings, the name and number
of the Lodge, and to display the Masonic Emblem in so doing.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes is of the opinion
that such newspaper advertisements are presently permissible, but it
is recognized that there may have been, and there may be, very strictly
construed interpretations of annotation "u" under Section 333 of the
C.M.C. It is. therefore, probably beneficial that action be taken by the
~ran~ Lodge :Vhich will leave. no question as to the propriety of a Lodge
msertmg a paid advertisement in a newspaper of general circulation to
publicize the name and number of the Lodge, where and when it meets,
and in so doing to use the Masonic Emblem to draw attention to the
advertisement.
I, therefore, move the adoption of Resolution No. 21 and your Committee recommends a "yes" vote.

The Committee on f urisprudence:
This resolution would authorize publication in a newspaper of general circulation of an announcement composed of the Masonic Emblem
and the name, number, address and meeting dates of a Lodge; joint
announcements by Lodges; and source of funds.
While there is at present no specific prohibition or authorization regarding such publication, in order to remove any uncertainty as to its
legality, the Committee proposes the following:
RESOLVED: That an annotation be added to Section 333 of the
California Masonic Code to read as follows: "A Masonic Lodge may,
if it so desires, cause to be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the area in which the Lodge is located, an announcement composed of the following: The Masonic Emblem, name and number of the
Lodge, address and dates of meetings. And further, a Lodge may jointly
:Vith another Lodge or Lodges meeting in the same temple, join together
m such an announcement. Cost of the announcement is to be defrayed
from the refreshment fund of the Lodge."
Adopted 5/6 vote.

To the. Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS. there is no present Ordinance or Policy of this Grand
Lodge respecting the display of the Masonic Emblem. the Square and
Compass, upon or adjacent to a Masonic Temple or a Lodge Hall, and
WHEREAS. it is not repugnant to Masonic principles for the
emblems of concordant Masonic organizations to be displayed in the
same general location as the Masonic Emblem.
NOW. THEREFORE. BE IT RESOLVED that this Grand Lodge
does hereby enact the following Ordinance to be added to Part II,
Article I of the California Masonic Code, Relative to Constituent
Lodges:
"Section 386. The Square and Compass may be displayed upon or
near a Masonic Temple or Lodge Hall in the same general location
which is used for the display of the emblems of the concordant Masonic
organizations. The Square and Compass may be displayed in any position with reference to any of the emblems of the concordant Masonic
organizations. whether such display is in the form of a circle. a horizontal line, a perpendicular line, or any other geometric pattern."
Respectfully submitted,
JAMES H. LEACH, P.M .. No. 35
Referred to Committees on Jurisprudence, and on Policy and General Purposes
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
There has been referred to your Committee on Policy and General
Purposes Resolution No. 24 which seeks to add to the ordinances of
Grand Lodge a new section relating to the display of the Square and
Compass upon or near a Masonic Temple or Lodge Hall when the
Square and Compass is to be placed in the same general location used
for the display of the emblems of concordant Masonic organizations.
The proposed new section further recites that the Square and Compass may be displayed in any position with reference to any of the
emblems of the concordant Masonic organizations, whether such display is in the form of a circle. a horizontal line, a perpendicular line,
or any other geometric pattern.
Your Committee notes that Masonic Lodges may be and, in fact.
are quartered in buildings sometimes owned by Lodges or Lodge Temple Associations. at other times by Masonic related organizations, or
by non-Masonic or other types of ownership.
We call attention to the difficulty, and in certain instances impossibility, of establishing regulations sufficiently broad enough to cover the
entire range of placement of our Masonic emblems on buildings owned

The Committee on Jurisprudence:
Your Committee on Jurisprudence presents the following resolution
to carry out the intended purpose of the proposer of Resolution No. 24.
RESOLVED: That this Grand Lodge does hereby enact the following Ordinance to be added to Part II, Article I of the California Masonic
Code. Relative to Constituent Lodges:
"Section 334.1. The Square and Compass may be displayed
upon or near a Masonic Temple or Lodge Hall in the same general location which is used for the display of the emblems of the
concordant Masonic organizations. The Square and Compass may
be displayed in any position with reference to any of the emblems
of the concordant Masonic organizations, whether such display is
in the form of a circle, a horizontal line, a perpendicular line, or

The Committee on Jurisprudence:
This resolution was referred to the Committee on Jurisprudence
which reports as follows:
This resolution proposes to permit Lodges to observe and respect
the wish of a departed Brother or his family that contributions be made
in lieu of flowers.
The proposed resolution requires the amendment of Section 411 by
an addition to the second paragraph.
In addition, annotations 409m and n in broad terms prohibit such
charitable contributions. The proposed resolution to be acted upon
today, unless it includes language deleting annotations 409m and n,
creates an inconsistenc•y. The Committee, therefore, believes that to accomplish the purpose of Resolution No. 26 annotations 409m and n
shou Id be deleted.
The following resolution would accomplish the expressed purpose
of Resolution No. 26:
RESOLVED, that Section 411 be amended by adding at the end
of the flrst sentence of the second paragraph the words, "or any charitable or philanthropic fund. society, association, foundation, church.
lodge building or scholarship fund," and by amending the last sentence
of the second paragraph by deleting the words. "Such donation," and
substituting therefor the words "A donation to the Masonic Homes
Endowment Fund.''
IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED that annotations 409m and n
should be and are hereby deleted.
The Committee moves the adoption of the resolution.
A majority voted against the resolution.

WHEREAS. these quali6cations have continued through the ages
solely to maintain uniformity in ritual. which has excluded many men
of good character from joining our ranks. and
WHEREAS, the ritual is one of the tools which is used to teach
candidates the above tenets, and any workman worth his keep will
adapt bis tools to accomplish his purpose, and
WHEREAS, since we no longer work in operative Masonry, but
speculative only, the stringent physical requirements are contrary to
the fundamental principles of Masonry.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that section 511 of the California Masonic Code be amended to read as follows:
"511. Moral and physical qualifications. An applicant for the degrees of Masonry must be a man; no woman or eunuc~; fre~ born,
being neither a slave nor the son of a bond woman; a be~1ever m G~d
and a future existence: of moral conduct; capable of readmg and writing ; having no maim or defect in his body except the loss of limb or
limbs or other impairment which can be remedied with aid of a prosthesis, thereby rendering him capable of learning the art, and physically
able to conform substantially to what the several degrees respectively
require of him."
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that section 512 be amended to
read as follows :
"512. Sound discretion required. The question as to the physical
sufficiency of the applicant shall be left to the sole discretion of the
Lodge. When the applicant is unable to comply literally with the physical requirements without the aid of the prosthesis. the Master shall
state nature and extent of his disabilities to the Lodge before the ballot
is taken, and any prosthesis that is usually worn or used by the applicant for the performance of his daily tasks may be used by him to
qualify himself for the physical requirements and they shall at once be
considered an actual part of the physical structure of the body, and no
discrimination shall be made where this is an issue."
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that annotations 512( a). (c).
(h) and (i) be and the same are hereby deleted.
Respectfully submitted,
JACK T . EsTOLL, M., No. 226
RALPH W. GAINES, P.M., No. 226
EARL A. DAVIS, P.M.• No. 226

PHYSICAL QUALIFICATION
(28)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A . M . of California:
WHEREAS, Brotherly Love, Relief and Truth are the principal
tenets of our fraternity, and
WHEREAS. our present physical quali6cations adopted of necessity for the protection of the Brethren when operative Masonry was
in force, and

The Committee on Ritual:
Your Committee on Ritual, to which was referred Resolution No.
28 proposing the elimination of the requirements of physical quali6cation or modification of our existing requirements, has carefully con-

294

295

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIJ\

sidered this prop~sal. We have considered it without emotion and only
from the standpoint of what in our opinion would be good for Masonry.
Resolutions to reduce the physical qualifications of applicants have
come before this Grand Lodge regularly. in recent years particularly,
and all have been defeated by votes of the Brethren. In 1961, 1962
I 963. 1964. I 967 and I 968 such resolutions were opposed by the Rituai
Committee, and were defeated overwhelmingly in each instance.
This proposal is practically identical to Resolution No. I 8 presented
and acted upon at our 1968 Annual Communication. This resolution
was defeated by written ballot. It required a 5/ 6 majority, but received
only a 3/7 favorable vote.
Masonry selects its cc:indidates and admits them only after careful
investigation and a unanimous ballot. No one has a right to become a
Mason. It is a privilege granted to a comparatively small number.
To begin with , we exclude half of the human race. No woman can
become a Mason. Half of the remainder of the population is likewise
excluded, namely anyone under the required age of 21 years. In California , for more than one hundred years. we have adhered to the regulation that no one having a maim or defect in his body that may render
him incapable of learning the art and physically unable to conform to
what the several degrees respectively require of him, can become a
M ason.
The physical requirements for qualification of candidates for the
degrees of Masonry are probably as old as Masonry itself. They are
a su rvival of Operative Masonry and a re peculiar to the Masonic institution, just as are the regulations excluding women and minors. One
of the Ancient Landmarks stated by Dr. Mackey. and which for several
decades has been printed in the Ross Digest and our M asonic Code.
is the "qualification of candidates for initiation." as the 18th Landmark.
A natural sympathy for those unfortunate men who have suffered severe physical injuries has caused numerous propsals to change the old requirements, and these have been presented throughout the history of
our Grand Lodge. They have been rejected except for the compromise
which resulted in the adoption of our present regulations many years
ago, now contained in Sections 511 and 512 of the C.M.C.: "having
no maim or defect in his body that may render him incapable of learning
the art, and physically able to conform substantially to what the several
degrees respectively require of him." The question as to phys ical sufficiency of the applicant is left to the sound discretion of the Lodge, and
it is determined by the ritual.
Since the rule as to physical qualification has existed for so long
that it is at leas t regarded as one of the Ancient Lmdmarks it should
not be changed without some change in the condition of the Craft which
would compel it. We may properly inquire what change has occurred
in the condition of the Craft which would now require a change in our

ancient regulation. We know of none. Masonry does not go out and
seek candida tes; we select those who apply. and they must apply of
their own free will and accord.
If these proposals were adopted, it would require a different ritual
for each case of physical defect. depending upon the nature and severity
of the particular deformity. This would completely destroy any unifonnity in the ritual. Under our law. the conferrinrJ of a degree must
be in conformity with the es tablished ritual taught by the Grand Lecturer. and the conferring of a degree in a merely symbolic manner is
out of the question. ( C.M.C. Section 512-j.) Unless we are prepared
to do away with uniformity of the ritual. carefully built up for a century.
and prescribed by Sections 554 and 555 of the C.M.C., we cannot
change the rule as to physical qualifications. This proposed legislation
does not purport to change Sections 554 or 555 of the Code.
In our opinion, this Grand Lodge has already gone as far in meeting
physical insufficiency as it can reasonably go. making it depend upon
the applicant's ability to conform substantially to what the ritual may
require of him.
We disapprove the resolution and urge a "no" vote.

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution No. 28, referred to the Committee on Policy and General
Purposes. proposes amendment of Sections 511 and 512 of the California
Masonic Code and relates to the admission of applicants for degrees
who have suffered the loss of a limb or limbs or other impairments which
can be remedied with the aid of a prosthesis. thereby rendering such
applicants capable of learning the art and physically able to conform
substantially to the requirements of the several degrees. It is practically
in the same language and to the sa me purpose as Resolution No. 18
considered and recommended favorably by the Committee on Policy
and General Purposes but failed a majo rity vote at the last convocation
of this Grand Lodge in 1968.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes has thoroughly
discussed this resolution on several occasions but was unable to reach
unanimous agreement. This report, therefore, represents the majority
opinion and recommendation only.
The majority of the Committee is of the opinion that the reasoning
expressed by the Committee on Policy and General Purposes, and which
is printed on page 268 of the 1968 Proceedings. is not only still valid
and compelling but has been made even more so by the passage of time
and the events thereof during which man daily runs the risk of losing
what we term his "physical qualifications." As it refers to the 1968 resolution and commencing immediately following the introductory paragraph it reads as follows:
''This resolution presents a direct confrontation between the
requirements of traditional regula tions and fundamental Masonic

296

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

principles. In bala~ce and stark contrast stand the tenet of Brotherly
Love and the requirements of present Masonic law.
The fact that our present rule has existed for a long period of
time establishes no case for its merit. Rather, the fact that almost no
Mason feels entirely comfortable with this regulation makes timely
and thorough examination of its merits highly desirable.
All men are captives of their corporeal beings, and stand in constant risk of debilitating and humiliating injury. Accident and unfortunate happenstance cast a dark enough shadow across the
lives of us all. No man or group of men should add to this burden
without having serious and compelling reasons so to do.
That our rules as they now stand add to the already frightful
burden of the maimed and injured is beyond question. With the rejected applicant, the effect is direct and immediate. But all men embraced within the ambit of our rules are poorer as a result. Only the
strongest reasons should cause us to add the weight of disqualification to all of the uncertainties and self-doubts associated with
serious injury.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes believes that
such compelling reasons do not exist. With the aid of modern prosthetic science, seriously injured persons can perform tasks that require great agility and dexterity. Many men who have suffered the
loss of a limb or limbs, or other physical injury, can substantially
(and in some cases fully) comply with the requirements of our degrees. These men in our opinion should be able to participate in our
privileges.
These new applicants would doubtless benefit from a Masonic
affiliation. Our Lodges would have a new source of interest and
strength. Most importantly, we would stand taller as men and
Masons by so providing."
Except for the recommendation for an affirmative vote this ends
the Committee's 1968 report on this subject.
'
The Committee on Jurisprudence authorizes this Committee to report that the proposed amendments would accomplish the purpose of
the proponents and, therefore, will not make any report thereon.
The majority of your Committee on Policy and General Purposes
moves the adoption of this resolution and recommends an affirmative vote.
A majority voted against the resolution.

MULTIPLE CANDIDATES-CONFERRING OF DEGREES
(29)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, the 1963 report on the Special Commission of Masonic
Practices likened our Fraternity to a "reposing titan"-having a great
potential and questioned how to transform this potential strength into
a vigorous force for good, and
WHEREAS, our efforts are stultified or as one PGM wrote, the
Craft "suffers from some fraternal hardening of the arteries, and
WHEREAS, we are no longer able to obtain leaders of high caliber
the progressive line is many times wea kened by those who quit because
of other interest, and
WHEREAS, investigation has shown that sojourners are left cold
and uninterested, and
WHEREAS, the problem of non-attendance and apathy is fed by
the "sheer frequency of meetings," "especially where there is a high factor of repetition of activity," which reduces the meaning thereof even
as TV cigarette commercials waste themselves away by repetition, and
WHEREAS, to combat absenteeism, pleas have been made for
more Lodge-related social activties: "they dearly evidence a realization
that the day of the traditional 'men' s house' has passed," and
WHEREAS, more enthusiasm must be generated for our Public
Schools Observance, Constitution Observance, etc .. and
WHEREAS, there is an overbearing burden on the Lodge members,
particularly the officers to meet once a week or more to be able to accomplish the "work," and
WHEREAS, QUALITY rather than QUANTITY is being
stressed, and
WHEREAS, our Lodges have come to be regarded, in public and
private, as DEGREE MILLS, operating merely for the sake of necessary repetition; an entire day or night of repeating the same degree with
little if any participation by the handful of sideliners, and
WHEREAS, meetings less frequent would realease us f.rom "going
because I have to be there" to "going because I want to be there," and
WHEREAS. even the Churches, as evidenced by the ecumenical
movement, have recognized that archaic practices and doctrines must
be changed to keep the Church viable so must the Grand Lodge recognize that we too, have these same problems, and
WHEREAS, by reducing the number of meetings thus saving PRECIOUS TIME for fraternization at refreshment; lodge related social
activities, Public Schools observance, etc .. would promote greater attendance among the Brethren, we suggest and pray that the Grand
Lodge will consider the wisdom of putting up to flve candidates for any

298

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRA ND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

The Committee on Ritual:
Your Committee on Ritual opposes this resolution on the basis
stated in the Report of the Committee on Policy and General Purposes
wherein references were enumerated in regard to the difficulties to be
encountered in the conferring of multiple degrees and on the basis that
such legislation would be contrary to C.M.C. Sections 554 and 555, and
the comments made in the Report of the Committee on Jurisprudence
relative to the preservation of our established ritual.
We strongly urge a "no" vote.
The Committee. on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution No. 29 proposes to amend section 525 of the California
Masonic Code to make it permissible to conduct up to five candidates
at one time through the ceremonies of our degrees.
The "whereas" clauses which precede the language of the proposed
amendment are numerous and contain numerous phrases enclosed in
quotation marks without disclosing the source from which the quotation
was derived or the remainder of the several texts from which the quo-

299

This committee does not believe that the answer to the issue can
be based upon an assertion that to adopt the amendment would be a
violation of basic Masonic law because the proposal is to a mend our
basic law, the California Masonic Code . which contains our constitution
and all of our ordinances. Nor can it be said that to adopt the proposed
amendment would be a violation of some body of law above or superior
to our Code which binds all Grand Lodges because such contention
is equivalent to charging the Grand Lodges of New York and Michigan
and perhaps others with being violators of basic M asonic law or principles for in these two jurisdictions (and perhaps others) as many as fi ve
candidates may and are conducted at one time.
Likewise, the answer does not lie in the field of ritual because
from time to time our Grand Lodge has made changes; for example,
about 1910 when the second section of the third degree was first adopted
in the form which we now use to begin that part. Any such r itualistic
premise is also answered by pointing to the fact that at least the Grand
Lodges of New York and Michigan have experienced no difficulty in
making their rituals conform to their law.
We must look elsewhere to determine whether this proposed amendment should be adopted or not adopted. We believe that the answer
is to be found outside the field of law or ritual. in fact the very reason
for which the ritual exists-the impression made upon the candidate.
It must be reco gnized that the proposed amendment would not
affect the second section of our fi rst degree. It wou Id not affect the
second section of our second degree. It would not affect the lecture of
the th ird degree. It wo uld not save what the proponents have capitalized
in their proposal. " PRECIOUS TIME," as to these substantial portions of our degree ceremonies.
The amendment would save time in the receiving of up to five candidates instead of one, just inside the door. Since the doors in most
Lodges are none too wide and the pillars are not spaced far apart, the
reception could be made in a column five deep, if the Stewards had, say,
eight assistants and the Senior Deacon had four good assistants. but
is the time saved worth it? A little later time could be saved if five declarations of faith were made at the same time . but is it worth it? F ive
candidates could be obligated at the altar if Lodges obtained wider
altars and placed five Bibles along the more extended altar. If time is the

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

GRAND LODGE OP CALIPORNIA

criteria, it might be necessary to provide up to four assistant Senior
Wardens to get the candidates kneeling for they certainly could not
see what they were doing. We could continue pointing out how time
could be saved by five candidates at a time in the first section of both
the first and second degrees but it would not be a reduction to onefifth the present time required for we doubt that five candidates can be
moved, caused to kneel and so forth in the same time as one candidate.
Even if we would save a number of minutes in reciting the obligations
only once, that same question bobs up to plague us: Is it really worth it?
When we turn to the second section of the third degree we would
either have to station up to five men in the southwest or east or we
would have to have one blindfold and allow candidates two through
five to be merely observers of what is occurring.
Oh yes. my Brethren, it could be done, it is not impossible to perform, but that blasted question won't go away-Would it be worth it?
That question you will have to answer. Your Committee on Policy
and General Purposes can do no more than recommend that you vote
"no" on the proposed amendment.

The Committee on furisprudence:
Resolution No. 29 proposes to amend Section 525 C.M.C. so that
by inference it will permit the conferring of degrees on more than one
candidate at one time.
This resolution is not only contrary to the ritual established in this
Grand Lodge from its very inception but it is contrary to Section 554
C.M.C. which requires conformity to the ritual taught by the Grand
Lecturer and recognized by Grand Lodge.
It is contrary to Section 555 C.M.C. which has almost the force of
a Landmark that the Grand Lodge alone has power to authorize changes
in the ritual. but, and we quote, "for the purpose of having it remain

This resolution obviously is not for the permitted purpose and we

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes believes that, as
stated in Annotation h under Section 577, a member should not be relieved of the duty to pay dues merely because a certain number of years
has been satisfied. The provisions relating to "10 year Masons and 75
year old Masons having dues remitted were intended for distinguished
service and to be applied only in those marginal cases where there may
be ability to pay but where a hardship still would be worked. Every
member should consider it a high privilege to help bear the costs of his
own Lodge and of the Grand Lodge.

LIFE MEMBERSHIP-FIFTY YEAR MEMBER
(34)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M . of California:
WHEREAS, there are many fifty year members of this jurisdiction
unable to pay dues because of fixed income, age, increased cost of living,
ill health, unable to attend Lodge and other hards hips, and
WHEREAS, these brethren who have fifty year membership in
this jurisdiction and have paid their dues regularly for this time, and
WHEREAS, they deserve this recognition, and be free of dues
but to donate to the Homes Endowment Fund if they so desire instead,
and
WHEREAS. this is a practice in some of the other jurisdictions to
relinquish dues to fifty year members, with no cost to the Lodge or
Grand Lodge, thus giving notice that when a member receives this commendation it creates a deep satisfaction to others to obtain this goal. and
WHEREAS, in many cases these monies were donated much earlier, to pay off mortgages, buy necessities, etc .. when monies were more
plentiful, and instead of taking a desired Life Membership, and
WHEREAS, "the remission of dues to a fifty year member would
add an incentive and avoid disappointment to our other Brethren attaining fifty years of Masonry and approve their image in the community in which he lives, and
WHEREAS. the feeling of the brother who reached this achievement is in his heart gratified that he has obtained this recognition and
just reward , and
WHEREAS, his feeling and past membership has been most gratifying.
NOW BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the necessary
deletions, additions and amendments be made to the appropriate sections of the California Masonic Code to provide for automatic remission
of said dues in advance to all Master Masons under this jurisdiction
who have received or who are entitled to receive a fifty year button
from the Grand Lodge of California.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON FINANCE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. 6 A. M. of California:
In accordance with the requirement of our Code, an audit of the
finances of Grand Lodge, the Masonic Homes of California and the
California Masonic Temple, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1969,
was completed. Copies of the audits, including that for the California
Masonic Foundation, have been reviewed by this Committee.
Our accounts are audited by a firm of Certifiied Public Accountants
of national and international standing. These audits follow procedures

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

consistent with practices approved by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants. The details are at all times on hand in the
Grand Lodge office and are available for inspection by any member of
Grand Lodge.
In the audit report for Grand Lodge, specifically the Exhibit titled
"Statement of Cash Revenues and Expenses." there is indicated an
evcess of revenue amounting to $124.179.00. comprised of a $38,477.00
gain realized on the sale of securities and a net revenue gain of $85,702.00
resulting from Grand Lodge operations.
Our net revenue gain is $27,000.00 less than net revenue gain for
the year previous. Total cash revenue for the past fiscal year dropped
by approximately $45,000.00 and most of this. or $32,000.00, re~ulted
from a lower per capita base. There was a decrease of 12 cents. m the
per capita assessment as between 1968 and 1969 but. of more importance, a decline in the assessable membership from 238,302 to 236.142
as of June 30, 1968.
Another major reduction in income this past year was caused by
the transfer of the expenses of the Endowment Board from the Masonic
Homes to Grand Lodge. This policy change accounted for a $12.000.00
decrease in revenue.
The cost to operate Grand Lodge last year showed a decrease of approximately $18,000.00 from the previous year, spread throughout the
Administrative and General Expense categories and in the Appropriations. As to Appropriations. it will be noted that practically all Committees, twenty-two out of a total of twenty-six. incurred expense~ this
past year well within their budgeted amounts; only four committees
exceeded their budgets by less than $1,300.00 total.
Necessary supplemental appropriations covering items for which
budgets had not been provided, or were insufficient, totaled $30,083.00.
Included in this $30,083.00 are two major items- the unanticipated carrying cost of the Clubhouse at Los Angeles amounting to $9.575.00 in
excess of budget. and the absorption by Grand Lodge of the Endowment Board expenses and the Wednesday trip to our Decoto Home
totalling $12,890.00, an amount not budgeted by the Masonic Homes
Trustees. All supplemental items were duly approved by the Grand
Master and we recommend your approval of his action.

the past. we express our sincere appreciation of the splendid service
which our Grand Treasurer continues to render so unselfishly to this
Grand Lodge.

GRAND TREASURER'S REPORT

The Report of the Grand Treasurer was referred to and reviewed
by this Committee. We find all reported items to be in accord with the
audit reports and we recommend your approval.
The report reflects the diligence and the competence of our Gran~
Treasurer, Paul A. Pflueger, in his supervision of the finances and capital funds of Grand Lodge and its agencies. As has been said so often in

313

COMMENTS RELATIVE TO PROPOSED BUDGET

New procedures whereby certain expenses of Grand Lodge officers
and committeemen are reimbursable have created a difficult task for all
concerned. Obviously a major expense has to do with attendance at the
Annual Communication. The provision for expense reimbursement was
estimated last October at 35 cents per capita and time did not allow for
specific allocation to committees and other categories. Our budget for
the ensuing year includes the best estimate by your officers and Committee Chairman of necessary and reasonable items of expense, and the
allocation of amounts has been made to the respective categories. It
now appears that the total cost of this provision for expense reimbursement amounts to approximately 50 cents per capita.
As a result of a survey made by the Grand Lodge Committee on
Insurance, new policies were written effective July 1, 1969. covering
our insurance needs. The three year premium, amounting to $135.000.00 for Grand Lodge and its agencies, will need to be paid in one
sum. In line with past pradice, one-third of the Grand Lodge premium
is being included in this year's budget and the .r emainder will be absorbed in the budgets for the following two years.
We call attention of this Grand Lodge to items designated as compensation included m the California Masonic Code. particularly the
payments being made to the Grand Lecturer, Organist. Grand Tiler
and possibly others. We believe there is some question regarding the
status of these items as distinguished between the area of compensation
or salary with its related accountability requirements and the area of
reimbursable expenses. We urge that the committee referred to in the
Grand Master's Recommendation No. 4 promptly direct its attention
to this matter.
Reports of the Board of Trustees and Superintendents of the Masonic
Homes were reviewed with considerable interest. These reports indicate continuing. commendable progress in caring for our unfortunate
Brethren and their families as. for example, the lifting of quota restrictions based on size of Lodges. the modification of our building facilities
to enable the admission of non ~ambulatory persons, etc.
We are pleased to note that. notwithstanding increasing inflationary
costs and the above-mentioned improvements. the Homes have operated
this past year well within their income. Accordingly. The Board of Trustees has reduced the request for contributions by Lodges to an amount
of $1.00 per member. a 15 cent reduction in per capita requirements for
that purpose, and we heartily concur with this recommendation.

CORRESPONDENCE REPORT
ANNOUNCE MENT
Reviews of the Proceedings of other Grand
Lodges have appeared quarterly in the "California Freemason," copies of which have been sent
to each Grand Lodge. This program will be continued.
The "California Freemason" is issued quarterly
and each copy carries additional reviews. Hence,
they do not appear in these Proceedings.
